title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 4-6). Grothendieck wants an integral, divided-power (pd) analogue of Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial de Rham forms on simplices, nabla_n = Q[t_0..t_n,dt_i]/(sum t_i - 1, sum dt_i).

Why the naive version fails (p.4). Over Z with pd polynomials one cannot impose sum X_i = 1. The element 1 - sum X_i does not lie in the pd ideal, so X_n cannot be eliminated.

The fix. Take a coefficient ring S with a pd ideal J and a parameter t in J. Define
C_DRpd[n](S,J,t) = S{X_0..X_n}[dX_0..dX_n] / (sum X_i - t, sum dX_i)_pd.
This is the de Rham complex of a 'pd-infinitesimal simplex' sum X_i = t.

This page:
(1) Justification. In S{X_i}[dX_i] the ideal of forms whose augmentation lies in J carries divided powers. So dividing by the pd ideal generated by sum X_i - t and sum dX_i makes sense. The quotient is (S{X_i}/(sum X_i - t)_pd) tensor_S Lambda*(S^{[n]}/diag).
(2) Structure. It is a graded-differential, anticommutative (strictly alternating) S-algebra in degrees >= 0. It has an augmentation C_DRpd[n] -> S/J, with divided powers on the augmentation ideal compatible with d. The left margin records d(X^{[i]}) = X^{[i-1]} dX.
(3) Elimination. Since t - sum_{i<n} X_i lies in the pd ideal, X_n can now be eliminated. So C_DRpd[n] is isomorphic to S{X_0..X_{n-1}}[dX_0..dX_{n-1}].
(4) pd Poincaré lemma. That complex is a resolution of S: every pd form is exact via X^{[i-1]}dX = d X^{[i]}.
(5) Simplicial object. Letting n vary, [n] -> C_DRpd[n] is a simplicial pd cdga, functorial in (S,J,t). It is augmented to S/J = k and resolves S levelwise.
(6) Cochains. For a simplicial set X_* define C_DRpd(X_*; S,J,t) = Hom(X_*, C_DRpd*(S,J,t)), the analogue of Sullivan's A_PL. For a space X one uses the singular simplicial set S.(X).
(7) Caveat. One cannot say in general what its cohomology is. One only has a natural map H_DRpd(X_*; S,J,t) -> H*(X_*, S), and it is not an isomorphism functorially in X_*.

Next page. Specialisation to the universal case S = k{T}, J = augmentation ideal, t = T. This gives C ~= Gamma_k(Phi_k*) tensor Lambda(Psi_k*), a bigraded Koszul-type object built from the simplicial module of vertex functions.

Purpose. To find strictly commutative (pd) integral cochain models of homotopy types. This is the issue Sullivan solved over Q and which underlies Grothendieck's schematization question.
errors: The isomorphism should read S{X_0,...,X_{n-1}}[dX_0,...,dX_{n-1}] (n variables after eliminating X_n); the image shows X_{n-1}, and the machine transcription's X_n is wrong.

The comparison map H_DRpd(X_*) -> H*(X_*,S) is asserted without construction. It presumably comes from the Sullivan-style double complex C^p(X; C^q_*), whose columns are acyclic by the levelwise Poincaré lemma. The failure of iso corresponds to the failure of the row/extendability argument; integrally the degreewise simplicial modules (Gamma^m of the vertex-function module) have nontrivial homotopy, i.e. derived divided powers. This is not spelled out on the page.
Minor ambiguity: the object is first called a '1/2 simpliciale' resolution with augmentation; the variance wording (simplicial vs cosimplicial) is hesitant on the page.

ideas.what: pd de Rham complex of the 'simplex' sum X_i = t with t in a pd ideal J, as an integral substitute for Sullivan's polynomial forms
ideas.modern_name: integral / divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial cdga nabla_* (polynomial forms on simplices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) over Q; integral and finite-type variants by H. Cartan (1976), Cenkl-Porter (c. 1981); later Karoubi and others

ideas.what: pd Poincaré lemma: S{X}[dX] is a resolution of S, since d X^{[i]} = X^{[i-1]} dX
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma for the divided-power de Rham complex

ideas.what: Cochains C_DRpd(X_*) = Hom(X_*, C_DRpd*) for simplicial sets/spaces, with a comparison map to H*(X,S) that is not an iso integrally
ideas.modern_name: strictly commutative (pd) cochain models; obstruction to integral commutative cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan; Cartan; for the obstruction, Steenrod operations / Mandell's E-infinity theorem; Toën (affine stacks)
ideas.where_published: Theme related to schematization in Pursuing Stacks (1983), but this construction is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Universal parameter t (S = k{T}, t = T) producing a bigraded pd-Koszul object Gamma(Phi) tensor Lambda(Psi)
ideas.modern_name: pd-Koszul complex / Illusie-style décalage of Gamma and Lambda on simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent, 1971) for the décalage of Gamma and Lambda

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines an integral divided-power Sullivan-type cochain functor Hom(X_*, C_DRpd*(S,J,t)) on simplicial sets. He notes it maps to H*(X,S) but is not isomorphic to it, and leaves open what its cohomology is.
missed.quote: Mais on ne peut dire en général (on a seulement H_DRpd(X_*;S,J,t) -> H(X_*,S)) qu'elle est sa cohomologie
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Computing this cohomology (via derived divided powers of the vertex-function simplicial module) would describe exactly how pd-commutative cochains fail integrally. That ties to Toën's affine-stack schematization, Mandell's theorem and recent integral models of homotopy types. Grothendieck's explicit 'pd-infinitesimal simplex' with parameter t appears not to be credited to him.

missed.claim: The 'simplex' sum X_i = t with t in a pd ideal (rather than = 1) is a crystalline-style device. It links crystalline pd techniques to rational homotopy models of spaces.
missed.quote: les équations sum X_i = 1 de E^[n] par l'équation sum X_i = t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the use of pd/crystalline tools in integral and p-adic homotopy theory (e.g. Toën's 'schématisation revisité'). It is a precursor of that link, from 1975-76.

deep.surprise_reason: A deliberate 1975-76 construction by Grothendieck of an integral divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial de Rham algebra, with the parameter trick t in J and an explicit admission that it fails to compute integral cohomology. The individual ingredients are known (pd Poincaré lemma; Cartan/Cenkl-Porter integral variants), but this specific construction and its link to the schematization problem are not in the record under his name.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est une S-algèbre de ∫A gr. diff.' should be 'C'est une S-algèbre gr. diff. anticommutative'.
'pour 𝒳_* ∈ (Sch)' is likely 'pour 𝒳_* ∈ (Ss)' (simplicial sets), given Hom(𝒳_*, simplicial object).
'(et si X cosimpl[?]' is likely '(et si X espace top.', with S.(X) the singular simplicial set.
'ne se. pas isom' is probably 'ne se réduit pas' / 'n'est pas isomorphe (pour 𝒳_* variable) à H*(𝒳_*,S)'.
